profiles.summary: No ordinary account can make a deposit carry the PoolManager as sender (the portal upgrader can, see the OP Stack portal finding), and the announced upgrades keep transient storage per transaction and roll it back with the frame or phase.

deltas.delta: No account on Ethereum can make an OP Stack deposit carry the PoolManager as sender. OptimismPortal2 on develop keeps msg.sender as the deposit's from only when EOA.isSenderEOA holds (msg.sender == tx.origin, or 23 bytes of EIP-7702 delegation code) and aliases every other caller. On Ethereum at block 26,492,947 each of the seven PoolManager addresses has no code and nonce 0, and the address whose alias equals each PoolManager (PoolManager minus 0x1111000000000000000000000000000000001111) has no code and nonce 0. A deposit from the PoolManager would need the private key of that address or a contract created at the un-aliased address, which takes about 2^160 work.

Lagoon (not scheduled on 2026-11-25) adds a sequencer-built post-execution transaction (type 0x7D) carrying Sequencer-Defined Metering gas refunds. Its settlement moves ETH outside EVM execution, after a transaction's frame finishes: it credits tx.from and debits the base fee, beneficiary and operator fee vaults, bounded by the transaction's own gas used. It is not executed as code and cannot name the PoolManager, which never originates a transaction. Lagoon also installs the interop predeploys; SuperchainETHBridge.relayETH pays the recipient through a SafeSend contract that forces ETH in without calling it.

deltas.delta: Base's endpoint still reports base v1.5.6 (revm-interpreter 42.0.0, ruint 1.19.0); no later tag exists. The main branch moves to revm 43.0.3 with revm-interpreter 43.0.2 and keeps ruint 1.19.0, and still builds BaseEvm on the stock EthInstructions table; the evm2 crate stays unwired. Between revm-interpreter 42.0.0 and 43.0.2 the instruction code changes in three places: CREATE checks call depth in the opcode, memory growth fails with MemoryOOG if the buffer cannot grow (SharedMemory::resize always returns true), and push_slice uses as_chunks in place of chunks_exact with the same split. None changes an arithmetic, comparison, shift, jump, hashing, copy, return data or transient storage result, and the PoolManager has no CREATE.

deltas.delta: No account on Ethereum can make an OP Stack deposit carry the PoolManager as sender. OptimismPortal2 on develop keeps msg.sender as the deposit's from only when EOA.isSenderEOA holds (msg.sender == tx.origin, or 23 bytes of EIP-7702 delegation code) and aliases every other caller. On Ethereum at block 26,492,947 each of the seven PoolManager addresses has no code and nonce 0, and the address whose alias equals each PoolManager (PoolManager minus 0x1111000000000000000000000000000000001111) has no code and nonce 0. A deposit from the PoolManager would need the private key of that address or a contract created at the un-aliased address, which takes about 2^160 work.

Everest (no date) brings Base Transactions (EIP-8430): phased batches of top-level calls from the sender in one transaction. In base/base main, each phase runs under a revm journal checkpoint that is reverted when any call of the phase fails (crates/common/evm/src/base_tx.rs lines 1243-1323); revm journals TSTORE as TransientStorageChange and restores it on checkpoint revert. Transient storage is not cleared between calls or phases, which is what a multicall contract already gets inside one transaction. Gas paid in tokens is an ordinary token transfer call in phase 0.

Denim (live on 5 November 2026) makes blocks every 200 ms while block.timestamp stays in whole seconds, so five consecutive blocks can share a timestamp and block.number runs ten times faster. The PoolManager bytecode reads neither TIMESTAMP nor NUMBER (OPCODES.md, bytecode inventory). Hooks or oracles that do are outside this cycle's scope.

cleared.check: Base Transactions (EIP-8430) phases against the transient storage model of the PoolManager (lead L-090, assumption A1).
cleared.result: A failing phase reverts its journal checkpoint, which restores TSTORE writes, and later phases are skipped; transient storage is shared across the calls of one transaction, as with a multicall contract. An unlock still has to finish inside one top-level call (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Token gas reimbursement is a normal transfer call. Read from main before activation; the shipped release must be reread.

cleared.check: Lagoon post-execution transaction and SDM refunds: balance moves outside EVM execution (assumptions A2, A3).
cleared.result: The settlement credits only tx.from and debits only fee vaults and the block beneficiary, bounded by the transaction's own gas used, and runs after the frame ends, so it cannot fall between a sync and a settle and cannot touch the PoolManager's balance.

relayETH forces ETH in through SafeSend without a call. Native settlement credits msg.value only (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354), so ETH forced into the PoolManager credits nobody and stays as surplus; no pool or claim balance moves. This is the F-137 bracket only for an ERC-20 path, which relayETH does not have.

cleared.check: EIP-7825 transaction gas cap on these chains and its effect on swaps (assumption A9).
cleared.result: Same cap as Ethereum for user transactions, and deposits are exempt up to their 20 million gas guarantee. A swap too heavy for one transaction can be split with price limits and a liquidity removal has no loop over other ticks (OPCODES.md, cycle 18), so the cap delays without loss, as recorded in F-064. Simulated calls ignore the cap on all seven endpoints, which earlier scripts must be read with.
